articles.title: Microsoft is officially killing its Outlook Lite app next month
articles.description: Launched in 2022, Outlook Lite is a lightweight version of the regular Outlook app, designed for Android phones with limited storage and regions with slower internet connections. The app had already been scheduled for retirement.

digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### How to make Firefox builds 17% faster
URL: https://blog.farre.se/posts/2026/04/10/caching-webidl-codegen/
One-line subtitle — WebIDL codegen caching delivers meaningful compile-time wins for Mozilla's build infrastructure.
A 17% improvement in build times directly impacts developer velocity and CI/CD costs at scale. This matters beyond Mozilla—the technique applies broadly to any project with heavy code generation steps. For infrastructure-heavy orgs, build optimization compounds into real OpEx savings.

### N-Day-Bench – Can LLMs find real vulnerabilities in real codebases?
URL: https://ndaybench.winfunc.com
One-line subtitle — First rigorous benchmark for measuring LLM capability in vulnerability discovery.
This fills a critical gap in AI security tooling evaluation. As companies integrate LLMs into security workflows, having standardized benchmarks prevents snake-oil purchases. The results will likely show current models underperform marketing claims—useful signal for security teams evaluating AI-assisted code review tools.

### DuckLake v1.0 – The Lightweight Lakehouse Format Reaches Production-Readiness
URL: https://ducklake.select/2026/04/13/ducklake-10/
One-line subtitle — DuckDB ecosystem continues expanding into enterprise data infrastructure.
DuckDB's lakehouse format hitting 1.0 signals maturing competition for Databricks and Snowflake at the storage layer. The lightweight positioning targets cost-conscious teams who don't need full managed solutions. Watch for adoption in mid-market analytics stacks.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch signals IPO readiness as AI agents fuel revenue surge
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/vercel-ceo-guillermo-rauch-signals-ipo-readiness-as-ai-agents-fuel-revenue-surge/
One-line subtitle — AI-generated apps are driving infrastructure demand to the point of IPO viability.
Vercel's positioning as the deployment layer for AI-generated code is proving out. When agents write apps, those apps need hosting—Vercel captures that demand without building AI itself. Classic picks-and-shovels thesis validated. IPO timing suggests they're seeing sustained, predictable growth.

### Microsoft exec suggests AI agents will need to buy software licenses, just like employees
URL: https://www.businessinsider.com/microsoft-executive-suggests-ai-agents-buy-software-licenses-seats-2026-4
One-line subtitle — Microsoft floats per-agent licensing as the enterprise monetization model for AI.
This is the first concrete signal of how incumbents plan to capture AI agent economics. Per-seat licensing scaled to agents could multiply enterprise software TAM dramatically—or trigger procurement warfare. Vendors without agent-aware pricing will face arbitrage pressure.

### Slate Auto raises $650M to fund its affordable EV truck plans
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/slate-auto-raises-650m-to-fund-its-affordable-ev-truck-plans/
One-line subtitle — TWG Global doubles down on affordable EV trucks despite compressed margins industry-wide.
$650M is a large bet given EV truck economics remain challenging. Mark Walter's continued backing suggests either proprietary cost advantages or a longer-term strategic play. Competition with Rivian and legacy OEMs will test whether "affordable" and "profitable" can coexist in this segment.

### IBM pays $17M fine to end DOJ suit over DEI programs
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/ibm-pays-17m-fine-to-end-doj-suit-over-dei-programs/
One-line subtitle — DOJ enforcement action creates precedent risk for enterprise DEI programs.
The $17M settlement is immaterial to IBM's balance sheet but material to corporate legal strategy broadly. Expect accelerated DEI program restructuring across tech as general counsels reassess litigation exposure. This shifts from voluntary rollbacks to legally-driven ones.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Someone bought 30 WordPress plugins and planted a backdoor in all of them
URL: https://anchor.host/someone-bought-30-wordpress-plugins-and-planted-a-backdoor-in-all-of-them/
One-line subtitle — Supply chain attacks via plugin acquisitions expose fundamental trust model failures.
This is a textbook PE-style attack vector: acquire neglected software assets, inject malware, profit from existing install base. WordPress powers ~40% of the web, making plugin supply chains high-value targets. The remediation complexity here—identifying all affected sites—makes this particularly damaging.

### Hack at Anodot leaves over a dozen breached companies facing extortion
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/hack-at-anodot-leaves-over-a-dozen-breached-companies-facing-extortion/
One-line subtitle — Single vendor compromise cascades into multi-company extortion event.
Anodot's breach hitting Rockstar Games and others demonstrates concentrated third-party risk. Analytics vendors sit on sensitive operational data across multiple clients—breaching one yields a portfolio of targets. Due diligence on vendor security posture is no longer optional for portfolio companies.

### Stanford report highlights growing disconnect between AI insiders and everyone else
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/stanford-report-highlights-growing-disconnect-between-ai-insiders-and-everyone-else/
One-line subtitle — Public anxiety over AI jobs and healthcare is outpacing industry optimism.
The perception gap creates regulatory and political risk. When insiders dismiss concerns that voters hold strongly, policy responses tend to be blunt rather than nuanced. Companies should anticipate populist-flavored AI regulation, particularly around employment displacement.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The licensing question for AI agents is this week's most consequential signal—it reframes every SaaS business model and procurement negotiation. Meanwhile, supply chain attacks via acquisitions (WordPress plugins, vendor breaches) are moving from edge case to pattern. The orbital compute announcement is interesting but premature; 40 GPUs in space is a proof-of-concept, not infrastructure.
